items.title: the struct hint in a variable/field hover runs straight on from the `NAME: STRUCT` line, and sits ABOVE the doc comment: give it a gap, and put it at the bottom when other information (docs) is shown
items.body: The hover for a binding or field whose type is a struct prints `name: Struct` and then the `struct Struct { .. }` shape with no separation. Two changes: (1) a visible gap (its own fenced block, or a rule) between the signature line and the shape hint; (2) order: signature, then the doc comment, then the shape hint LAST - the hint is reference material, the docs are what the author wrote for this name. Pin both in the hover goldens.

items.discussion: owner 2026-10-03; F27 R1/R6 (`vilan/analysisPlatform`, the `analyzed as:` line); E106/E174 (session status); `editors/vscode/src/extension.ts`
items.title: the status bar line `analyzed as: ..` becomes `vilan {VERSION}`, and a click opens a MENU: the entry/platform facts, the last analysis' cost, and toggles for the common language options (inlay hints first)
items.body:
Today the status bar item prints `analyzed as: browser — declared` with the reason in its tooltip. The owner's shape: the item reads `vilan 0.43.0` (the server's version), and clicking it opens a menu.

Recommended build: a `StatusBarItem` with a command that opens a QuickPick (rust-analyzer's and TypeScript's pattern).

- Read-only rows: the platform and why (`analyzed as` moves here, and stays in the tooltip), the entry the file is analyzed under (M104's entry world, when it lands), the server version + sha, the last analysis of this file: wall time and the solver's work counts (M105's instruction-free counters; M106's complexity figures when they exist).
- Toggle rows: `vilan.inlayHints.enabled`, `.abbreviate`, and the other feature switches the server already reads per request - each row flips the setting through `workspace.getConfiguration('vilan').update(..)`, which the extension already pushes to the running server live (no restart). Scope: the workspace setting if one exists, else the user setting.
- Action rows: restart, stop/start (E248), show server status, open the output channel.

The status item turns to a warning colour when the server is stopped or crashed. Needs one new server request (or an extension of `vilan/analysisPlatform`) for the per-file cost figures.

items.title: command palette: `Vilan: Stop Language Server` and `Vilan: Start Language Server` - there is only Restart today, so a badly behaving server or a known-broken file cannot be silenced
items.body: Add `vilan.stopServer` and `vilan.startServer` beside `vilan.restartServer`. Stop disposes the client and does NOT auto-restart (including on configuration changes and on the crash-restart policy) until Start or a window reload; the status bar item says `vilan (stopped)`. Stale diagnostics are cleared at stop. Log E106's session status before stopping, as Restart does.

items.status: OPEN — filed 2026-10-03 (owner's item); probed on dcb06444
items.discussion: owner 2026-10-03; B486 (out-of-order marker steers); probes: `return 1;` → 'expected `;` to end this statement', `fn a()`/`function a()` → the same, `fun a() -> i32` → "found '-' expected '{' or ';'"
items.title: foreign spellings get no steer: `return EXP` (it is `ret`), `fn`/`function` (it is `fun`), `() -> T` (it is `(): T`) - each should say so, with a quick fix
items.body: Today all four fall into generic parse errors (see the probes), and `return 1;` also cascades a second 'body ends without producing a value' error. Wanted, in the parser's recovery: recognise the identifier `return` at statement head followed by an expression or `;`; `fn`/`function`/`def`/`func` at item head followed by a name and `(`; and `->` after a parameter list. Each reports ONE diagnostic at the foreign token - "vilan spells this `ret`" - parses on as if the right spelling had been written (so no cascade), and carries an LSP quick fix that rewrites the token (`->` becomes `:`). Candidates to consider in the same pass: `let mut` order mistakes, `=>` vs `->` in closures, `null`/`nil` for `None`, `else if` spellings. Add ledger rows.

items.kind: std::ui (S); design, recommendation in the body
items.discussion: owner 2026-10-03; A121 §6.1 (`View::autofocus` writes the attribute; `FocusScope::focus_initial` reads `[autofocus]`), B271; kolt `lib/overlay.vl`
items.title: `autofocus` on a dynamically inserted element makes Chromium log 'Autofocus processing was blocked because a document already has a focused element' once per page load - std writes the NATIVE attribute as its focus-scope marker
items.body:
Not a Chromium bug and not an ordering fault in the overlay. The HTML spec queues an inserted `[autofocus]` element as an autofocus candidate; the document flushes candidates once (then sets its 'autofocus processed' flag), and refuses when something already has focus - the opener button, here - which Chromium reports on the console. Hence exactly once per page load, on the first modal. Focus itself is taken by the focus scope (`focus_initial`), which is why everything works.

A121 §6.1's claim that the attribute 'costs nothing at runtime' for an inserted element is therefore slightly wrong: it costs this message, and on a page with NOTHING focused the native processing would also focus the element on its own clock (before the panel is visible it is refused; harmless but unplanned).

Recommendation: std's marker becomes `data-autofocus` - `View::autofocus()` and the element-syntax `autofocus` attribute on a view both write it, `focus_initial` reads `[data-autofocus]` (and still honours a hand-written native `[autofocus]`), and the SERVER render keeps dropping it as today. The native attribute stays available by its raw name for a `<dialog>`/popover, whose focusing steps do read it. Kolt changes nothing.
